messages:
customer-acme-bob: Hey team — since late last night our on-prem app traffic to Redwood is being routed to us-west. We're seeing 403 org-region-mismatch and much higher latency. Traceroute and public IP below. Can you advise?

support-ian: Thanks — can you paste the traceroute output and the public egress IP (whatismyip)? Also are you NATing on your proxy?

customer-acme-bob: Traceroute and ip below. We do NAT on our edge proxy (k8s node nat).
```
traceroute to api.redwood.com (3.120.45.2), 30 hops max:
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.4 ms
 2  192.0.2.1 (192.0.2.1)  1.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.5 (203.0.113.5)  12.4 ms
 4  3.120.45.2 (3.120.45.2)  312 ms

$ curl -sS https://ifconfig.co
203.0.113.110

Response headers from failed request (from app logs):
x-region: us-west-2
x-request-error: org-region-mismatch
```

ops-liz: Looks like your source IP is being SNATed to a 203.0.113.0/24 pool that our routing fabric associates with US region prefixes. When the egress is hairpinned through our peered hub, that NAT address lands in the US-prefixed pool and our smart-router routes to the closest matching region (us-west).

support-ian: Quick checks: on a host behind the proxy run `curl -sS https://ifconfig.co` and `sudo iptables -t nat -S | head` and paste results. Also, do you see X-Forwarded-For on requests? If not, origin IP is lost.

customer-acme-bob: iptables shows MASQUERADE on the proxy node: `-A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/16 -j MASQUERADE`. We don't set X-Forwarded-For at the proxy.

alex: Root cause candidate: MASQUERADE SNAT replaces source with pool ip (203.0.113.110) which matches a prefix tagged as us-west in our route-lookup. Two remediation paths:
1) Preserve source (no SNAT) so routing decision is based on original customer ASN/prefix, or
2) Use a SNAT pool prefix that is tagged eu-central and/or adjust BGP local-pref so eu prefixes are preferred for your tenant.

mia: Short term workaround: in your Private console add an egress override to force eu-central selection. Example (console > Networking > Egress Overrides) set region_preference: ["eu-central-1"] — that should route traffic to eu endpoints immediately while we fix NAT.

customer-acme-bob: Applied override, re-tested. Good: most calls now go to eu and latency ~60ms. Bad: some requests still 403. Headers show origin IP = 203.0.113.110 in Authorization binding check so auth service still rejects.

alex: Auth tokens are org-scoped and validation sometimes checks client IP binding. Because SNAT still exposes hub NAT IP in TLS session origin, some auth checks fail. Please enable forwarding of client IP: ensure your proxy sets `X-Forwarded-For` and our ingress respects that for auth-binding if you opt in. Also we can flip a short-term auth fallback — @ops-liz can coordinate.

ops-liz: I'll do two things: 1) change your proxy NAT to use our eu SNAT pool (SNAT 198.51.100.0/29) and 2) adjust BGP local-preference so eu prefixes for your tenant are preferred over hub-us. Rolling change now.

deploy-bot: Canary: applied SNAT pool swap for tenant acme (canary 1/3). Monitoring for 5m.

customer-acme-bob: After canary: all traffic to eu, latencies stable, no 403s. Thank you.

ops-liz: Root cause summary: on-prem proxy using MASQUERADE -> hub NAT pool address (US-tagged) -> our smart-router selected US region. Secondary auth failures due to token IP-binding to hub NAT IP. Fixes: convert MASQUERADE to explicit SNAT using eu NAT pool, set proxy to preserve X-Forwarded-For, and we updated route preferences (BGP local-preference) for your tenant prefixes.

mia: Follow-up action items: customer to enable X-Forwarded-For and disable cluster-level MASQUERADE where possible; ops to confirm BGP/local-pref changes and push RCA doc.

support-ian: Thanks everyone — marking as mitigated. We'll send a short RCA and recommended config snippets. If anything regresses ping this thread. :thumbsup:
